sections.html:
Tooele is the county seat of Tooele County, about 40 minutes southwest of Salt Lake City, on the western slope of the Oquirrh Mountains in Tooele Valley. The city sits at an elevation of 4,915 feet with views of the mountains and the Great Salt Lake.

Tooele County itself is huge. It covers 6,923 square miles, which makes it the second-largest county in Utah, and the Great Salt Lake Desert fills most of the western half. Most towns sit in the broad valley between the Oquirrh Mountains to the east and the Onaqui and Stansbury Mountains to the west. The state's history encyclopedia also lists Grantsville and Wendover among the county's towns.

The county's population was 26,601 in 1990, and Tooele City's own census count has since climbed to 35,742 in 2020. The valley is still a distinct place from the Salt Lake Valley next door, with its own schools, its own history and its own tax office.

sections.h2: How did Tooele start, and what shaped it?
sections.html:
Three families settled on a small stream south of today's city in September 1849, and Tooele City was incorporated on June 19, 1853. The valley was the traditional land of the Tooele Valley Goshute, and archaeology at Danger Cave shows people lived in the region by about 9000 years ago.

For most of the 1800s Tooele was a farm town of about 1,200 people. Mining and smelting changed that. The International Smelting and Refining Company built a smelter east of the city in 1909. It ran copper from 1910 and lead and zinc from 1912, and the work ended by 1972, when the site was torn down. A neighborhood called New Town in the eastern part of the city was built for many of the roughly 1,000 smelter workers.

In World War II the federal government acquired 25,000 acres south of the city for an ordnance depot, now the Tooele Army Depot. About 1,700 acres were annexed to the city in 1993. The former Utah Industrial Depot was sold in 2013 and renamed Ninigret Depot.

sections.h2: What jobs and employers shape Tooele?
sections.html:
Tooele's economy mixes mining, industry, defense and government. The county's own history notes that the 1993 decision to put Tooele Army Depot on a Defense Department closure list was a major blow to the local economy, and the depot property has since been reused for industry.

  • Kennecott Utah Copper runs the Bingham Canyon Mine on the other side of the Oquirrh Mountains.
  • EnergySolutions operates a waste-storage facility in Clive, west of the valley, and US Magnesium is described as the country's largest magnesium producer.
  • Cabela's has a distribution center on the west side of Tooele.
  • Tooele Industrial Depot manages former Army buildings now used for manufacturing, warehousing and offices.
  • Utah Motorsports Campus, northwest of the city, hosts auto, motorcycle, bicycle and kart racing.

Federal, state and county agencies also employ a good share of residents, and Dugway Proving Ground is in the county's military land to the west.

sections.h2: How does Tooele connect to Salt Lake City?
sections.html:
The main link is State Route 36 to Interstate 80, and traffic backs up there. KSL reported that SR-36 as the first I-80 exit for westbound drivers, one that can back up for hours after a storm or crash.

The Midvalley Highway, State Route 179, opened on October 30, 2021. It is about 4.5 miles long and joins SR-138 to I-80, letting drivers reach Erda and Grantsville without using SR-36. UDOT expected it to cut traffic at the I-80 and SR-36 interchange by 15% to 20%, or about 6,000 to 8,000 vehicles a day.

  • Tooele County grew 25% from 2010 to 2020, the fifth-fastest percentage growth among Utah counties, compared with 18.4% statewide.
  • The road opened with one lane in each direction; more lanes were planned without a set date.
  • A rail line, the Los Angeles and Salt Lake Railroad, came through the city in 1904.

sections.h2: What are the climate and school details for Tooele?
sections.html:
Tooele has a hot-summer, cold-winter climate with an average of 18.44 inches of precipitation and 75.3 inches of snow a year. The record high is 106 degrees from July 2000, and the record low is minus 16 degrees, set in February 1933 and again in December 1990.

Snowfall at that level puts real load on roofs, gutters and heating systems. Check attic insulation and ice damming before you list.

The Tooele County School District is headquartered in Tooele. Inside the city are 8 of the district's 16 elementary schools, 2 of 3 junior highs and 2 of 5 high schools, Tooele High and Blue Peak. Utah State University has a regional campus in the city, and the Tooele Applied Technology College is also here. Saint Marguerite Catholic School and Scholar Academy Charter School serve families who want other options.

sections.h2: How do Tooele County property taxes and appeals work?
sections.html:
Tooele County mails a Notice of Property Valuation and Tax Change at the end of July, and you have 45 days from receiving it, or until September 15, to appeal your value. Taxes are due November 30 under Utah Code 59-2-1331, and unpaid taxes after that date carry a penalty of 2.5% or $10, whichever is greater.

The assessor accepts four kinds of evidence, and a complaint that taxes are too high is not an accepted basis.

  • Sales of comparable properties before January 1 that sold for less than your value.
  • Your own purchase before January 1, shown with a settlement statement. Short sales, bank-owned and foreclosure sales generally need an appraisal.
  • An appraisal with an effective date within the year.
  • A written statement of a factual error, such as wrong square footage or garage type.

You can look at your property card in person Monday through Friday, 7 a.m. to 6 p.m.; the office does not give card details by phone. Utah exempts 45% of a primary residence's value, up to one acre, and the title company prorates the current year's bill at closing.

sections.h2: What do Tooele sellers usually need?
sections.html:
Tooele has both older neighborhoods, such as New Town, which was built for smelter workers, and newer areas where the city has added thousands of residents since 2020. The reasons for selling vary, but a cash sale works when you do not want to repair the house, manage showings or wait through a financing period.

We buy Tooele houses as-is, including houses with deferred maintenance, tenants or an unsettled estate. We make an offer, and you decide whether to take it.

faqs.q: How many people live in Tooele, Utah?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 42,270 residents as of July 1, 2025, up from 35,742 at the 2020 census. Tooele is the county seat of Tooele County.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Tooele, Utah?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau reports a median value of $381,400 for owner-occupied homes in Tooele for 2020 to 2024. This is a survey estimate for the whole city, so your house may be worth more or less.

faqs.q: When is the Tooele County property tax appeal deadline?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from receiving your valuation notice, or until September 15, to appeal. The county mails notices at the end of July.

faqs.q: How far is Tooele from Salt Lake City?
faqs.a: The city is about 40 minutes southwest of Salt Lake City. Most drivers use State Route 36 to Interstate 80, and the Midvalley Highway (SR-179) opened in 2021 to relieve that interchange.

faqs.q: Will you buy a Tooele house that needs repairs or has tenants?
faqs.a: Yes. We buy as-is, so you do not need to fix, clean out or stage the house. You can decline the offer at no cost.
